title: The subgroup generated by a face is saturated
statement: Let $Q$ be a commutative monoid, written additively, which is integral (its canonical map to its group completion $Q^{\rm gp}$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] is injective) and saturated ($ng\in Q$ with $g\in Q^{\rm gp}$ and $n>0$ implies $g\in Q$), and let $F\subseteq Q$ be a face, meaning a submonoid such that $a+b\in F$ with $a,b\in Q$ implies $a,b\in F$. Let $F^{\rm gp}\subseteq Q^{\rm gp}$ be the subgroup generated by (the image of) $F$, which is $\{a-b:a,b\in F\}$. Then $F^{\rm gp}$ is a saturated subgroup of $Q^{\rm gp}$, meaning that $ng\in F^{\rm gp}$ with $g\in Q^{\rm gp}$ and $n>0$ implies $g\in F^{\rm gp}$; equivalently, $Q^{\rm gp}/F^{\rm gp}$ is torsion-free.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.1--3.1.2, printed pp. 98--99; the face subgroup and torsion-free sharp characteristic used in the localization discussion.

proof.text: Let n>0 and g∈Q^{\rm gp} satisfy ng∈F^{\rm gp}. By the definition of the subgroup generated by F, choose a,b∈F with ng=a−b. Set h=g+b. Then n h=a+(n−1)b lies in F and hence in Q. Saturation of Q therefore gives h∈Q.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.2 and Remark 3.1.10(i), printed pp. 98--99 (fact used there without proof; argument written by the agent).

proof.text: Because h∈Q and n h∈F, the face condition implies h∈F: write n h=h+(n−1)h (with the second summand in Q) and apply the defining implication for a face. Thus g=h−b belongs to F^{\rm gp}. We have shown that n g∈F^{\rm gp} with n>0 implies g∈F^{\rm gp}, which is exactly saturation of the subgroup F^{\rm gp}; equivalently, an element of Q^{\rm gp}/F^{\rm gp} killed by a positive integer is zero, so this quotient is torsion-free.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.2 and Remark 3.1.10(i), printed pp. 98--99 (fact used there without proof; argument written by the agent).

split_report.summary: Replaced the empty proof by the direct face-and-saturation argument: write a positive multiple of g as a difference of two face elements, translate by one of them, use saturation to put the translate in Q, and use the face condition to put it in F. This proves both subgroup saturation and the equivalent torsion-free quotient statement. No child nodes are needed; all ingredients are the item's own definitions and hypotheses.
split_report.blueprint: The two steps realize the face-subgroup and torsion-free quotient assertion used in Expose VIII, 3.1.1--3.1.2 and in the proof of lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q122-072abc1c4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the unit sk-i-curve-zero, def-trf-fs-log-blowup (it defines P^gp), the citer lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening, the siblings face-localization-fs and face-localization-units, and ILO VIII 3.1.1-3.1.2 (p.98) and Remark 3.1.10(i) (p.99). The mathematics is correct. Step 1: from ng=a-b with a,b in F, put h=g+b; then nh=a+(n-1)b is in F, so h is in Q by saturation of Q. Step 2: nh=h+(n-1)h with both summands in Q, so the face condition gives h in F and g=h-b in F^gp. The quotient Q^gp/F^gp is torsion-free for the same reason. n=1 is covered. Both steps are elementary, uses=[] is correct, and no step leaves the unit's route. Small cases: N^2 and N^r with coordinate faces, and the saturated monoid {a+b even} with face N(2,0), all give torsion-free quotients. ILO 3.1.10(i)'s example N+mu2 minus (0,-1), which is not saturated, has torsion, so the saturation hypothesis is needed. Duplicates: no sec-trace-formula face/monoid node states this, a DAG-wide search for 'saturated subgroup' hits only the item and its citer, and a blueprint search gives 0 hits. There are no new nodes and no tool_uses. Two repairable faults, fixed in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-trace-formula/lem-trf-face-subgroup-saturated.json. (1) B2/B3: the statement never defined F^gp or 'saturated subgroup', although the report says it did. The fix adds both definitions, F^gp being the subgroup generated by the image of F, i.e. {a-b}. This matches the citer and does not change the meaning, since Q is integral.
